title: 1973 AHSME Problem 5
statement:
Of the following five statements, \(\mathrm{I}\) to \(\mathrm{V},\) about the binary operation of averaging (arithmetic mean),

\(\mathrm{I}.\) Averaging is associative

\(\mathrm{II}.\) Averaging is commutative

\(\mathrm{III}.\) Averaging distributes over addition

\(\mathrm{IV}.\) Addition distributes over averaging

\(\mathrm{V}.\) Averaging has an identity element

those which are always true are

solutions.text:
Let \(a*b=\frac{a+b}{2}.\) Commutativity is immediate. Also \[ \begin{aligned} a+(b*c) &=\frac{2a+b+c}{2}\\ &=(a+b)*(a+c). \end{aligned} \] so addition distributes over averaging.

Associativity fails because \[ \begin{aligned} (a*b)*c&=\frac{a+b+2c}{4},\\ a*(b*c)&=\frac{2a+b+c}{4}. \end{aligned} \] Averaging does not distribute over addition since generally \[ a*(b+c)\ne(a*b)+(a*c). \] Finally, an identity \(e\) would require \(\frac{e+a}{2}=a\) for every \(a,\) or \(e=a,\) which is impossible for a fixed \(e.\) Thus only \(\mathrm{II}\) and \(\mathrm{IV}\) always hold.

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Expand each proposed identity; one counterexample is enough to reject a property
